summary: Configured node1’s persistent firewalld policy. SSH is allowed from any address; TCP 9000 is accepted only from node2 (10.100.127.11) and rejected from all other sources. Persistence and behavior were verified through serial restarts of all three nodes.
actions_performed: Added ordered permanent and runtime firewalld rules for TCP 9000.
Verified node2 received HTTP 200 while node3 was refused, with SSH working from both.
Restarted node1, node2, and node3 individually and confirmed changed boot identities and recovery.
Removed the temporary port-9000 listener used for testing; the firewall configuration remains active and persistent.

evidence.requirement: Persistent firewall, unrestricted SSH, and ordered TCP 9000 policy
evidence.summary: Runtime and permanent configurations match; SSH is enabled in both; counters show traffic hitting both the node2 accept and catch-all reject rules.

evidence.requirement: TCP 9000 allowed from node2 and rejected from node3
evidence.summary: After node1 restart, node2 received HTTP 200 while node3 was refused; both received the node1 SSH banner.
Healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered firewalld, SSH, runtime rules, and persistent rules.
Healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID, recovered SSH, and restored permitted access to node1:9000.
Healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID, recovered SSH, and continued rejection from node1:9000.
